agent_notes: The superscription (שִׁיר הַמַּעֲלוֹת לְדָוִד) is verse 1 in the Hebrew, so the five English versions, which number it 122:0, put the opening line of the psalm at 122:1 as well. I translated the superscription and the line together as one verse, as the Hebrew has them.

STEPBible glosses בְּאֹמְרִים as 'in [those who] said'. I kept 'in those saying' in the literal layer, since the preposition bet after שָׂמַח is causal ('rejoice in/at'), and the participle is present-continuous rather than a past event; KJV and ASV 'when they said' flatten that. Also the Targum's 'ascents of the abyss' (מַסוּקִין דִתְהוֹמָא) is a distinct tradition about the Songs of Ascents; I mention it only as a tradition, not as the meaning here.

agent_notes: הַבְּנוּיָה is a passive participle with the article ('the built one'). Reading it as 'rebuilt' or 'built up' is a choice the Hebrew does not force; I kept it plain. The Targum and Rashi (citing Taanit 5a) read an earthly versus heavenly Jerusalem; the Targum text in the packet says so explicitly.

agent_notes: עֵדוּת לְיִשְׂרָאֵל is ambiguous: 'a testimony to Israel', or 'an ordinance for Israel' (ASV). I kept 'testimony' with a note that 'decree' is possible. The Hebrew lacks a verb, so the clause floats; I did not decide between 'it is a testimony' and 'as a testimony'.

Radak's two thrones (one for the Shekhinah, one for the monarchy) is cited as his, not endorsed.

agent_notes: חֵיל here is the outer rampart or glacis in front of the wall, the same word as in Lam 2:8 (cited by Metzudat Zion and Meiri in the packet). STEPBible says 'rampart'; KJV 'walls' and BBE 'inside your walls' blur the distinction between the outer rampart (חֵיל) and the main wall (חוֹמָה). I kept 'rampart'. YLT's 'high places' for אַרְמְנוֹת is not what the lexicon says: 'fortresses, citadels'.
